Recall that the Chebyshev distance is defined as

$$
{d}_{\infty }(a,b)=‖a-b{‖}_{\infty }
$$

where for an $N$-dimensional vector $v,$

$$
‖v{‖}_{\infty }=max(|{v}_{1}|,|{v}_{2}|,…,|{v}_{N}|).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}_{\infty }(a,b) & =‖a-b{‖}_{\infty } \\  & ={‖[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 7 \\ 4\end{aligned}]‖}_{\infty } \\  & =max(|-3-2|,|5-7|,|1-4|) \\  & =max(5,2,3) \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
